items.title: Marty Napoleon interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York, New York, January 16, 1999
items.q: I mean I remember even when Buddy DeFranco was fronting the Glenn Miller band

ctx.x: That was the popular music of the day, what you were playing.

But that’s beside the point. The point is even today, you listen to a Glenn Miller arrangement, and the music is so melodic and so beautiful. I mean I remember even when Buddy DeFranco was fronting the Glenn Miller band a friend of mine called me and he says, “Marty, would you like to go see the Glenn Miller band?” I says, “where? He’s dead.” He said, “no, but Buddy DeFranco’s got the band, they’re going to be at St. Regis Roof.” I said, “I’d love to.” He says, “you’re my guest.” And we went up there and I

swear to you the band, I mean the kids in the band were like 18, 19 years old, young kids because he couldn’t afford to get older guys. When the band started to play the theme I had a lump in my throat and I got tears in my eyes. Because I said, “I don’t care how you feel about the band, the music was so beautiful and so romantic and so melodic. And I don’t understand these kids today. Don’t they hear a melody? I mean can’t they hear something when it makes sense?
